answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond that is locked while it trades, like tending an orchard where every tree needs its own plot and seasons of care before it bears fruit. New identities start in a shared meadow with tiny transaction limits, and only graduate after a history of honest, verifiable work. A flood of fake identities therefore costs the attacker a bond and months of waiting per identity, while honest agents pass like a zephyr through a gate that charges nothing but patience and a good record.
